claims.text: WTaTiVZr is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each constituent element.
WTaTiVZr exhibits greater plastic strain than commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
WTaTiVZr exhibits greater toughness than commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
WTaTiVZr has a highly disordered and intrinsically heterogeneous microstructure with high lattice distortion.
Microstructural heterogeneity and lattice distortion create numerous dislocation-pinning sites in WTaTiVZr.
The disordered microstructure of WTaTiVZr facilitates grain-boundary sliding relative to pure tungsten.
The disordered microstructure of WTaTiVZr facilitates nanotwinning relative to pure tungsten.
The multielement composition disrupts the regular dislocation motion characteristic of pure tungsten.
Disrupted dislocation motion initiates alternative plastic-deformation pathways involving grain-boundary sliding and nanotwinning.
Grain-boundary sliding and nanotwinning distribute stress in WTaTiVZr.
Stress distribution through the proposed alternative deformation pathways delays failure.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher nanoindentation creep strain than pure tungsten at 1000–1200 °C.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit a lower effective creep activation energy than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will show more microstructural evidence of grain-boundary sliding than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will show more microstructural evidence of nanotwinning than pure tungsten.
The proposed comparison uses identical temperatures, strain rates, indenter geometry, atmosphere, and surface preparation for WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
The hypothesis is limited to the tested high-temperature range and may not apply under substantially different loading or environmental conditions.
